m31-5-3.title: Implicit Differentiation and Higher Derivatives, Part 1: Implicit Differentiation

cues.prompt: Find the slope of the tangent to $4x^{2} + y^{2} = 8$ at the point $(1, 2)$.
cues.working: $8x + 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{4x}{y}$. At $(1, 2)$: $-\dfrac{4}{2} = -2$.

m31-5-3-b.title: Implicit Differentiation and Higher Derivatives, Part 2: Products and Mixed Terms

cues.prompt: Find the slope of the tangent to $xy + y^{2} = 6$ at the point $(1, 2)$.
cues.working: $y + x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{y}{x + 2y}$. At $(1, 2)$: $-\dfrac{2}{1 + 4} = -\dfrac{2}{5}$.

m31-5-3-c.title: Implicit Differentiation and Higher Derivatives, Part 3: Higher Derivatives

m31-5-3-d.title: Implicit Differentiation and Higher Derivatives, Part 4: Patterns in Derivatives

cues.prompt: Find the 50th derivative of $\cos x$.
cues.working: The derivatives of $\cos x$ are $-\sin x$, $-\cos x$, $\sin x$, $\cos x$, repeating every $4$. $50 = 4(12) + 2$, so the 50th derivative equals the 2nd: $-\cos x$.

m31-5-3-e.title: Implicit Differentiation and Higher Derivatives, Part 5: Second Derivatives Implicitly

cues.prompt: For $y^{2} = x$, find $\dfrac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}$ at the point $(4, 2)$.

m31-6-1.title: Tangent Lines and Linear Approximation, Part 1: The Tangent Line

cues.prompt: Find an equation of the tangent line to $f(x) = x^{2} + 3x$ at $x = 1$.

m31-6-1-b.title: Tangent Lines and Linear Approximation, Part 2: Normal Lines

cues.prompt: Find an equation of the normal line to $y = x^{2}$ at $x = 1$.
cues.working: The point is $(1, 1)$ and the tangent slope is $2x = 2$. The normal slope is $-\dfrac{1}{2}$: $y - 1 = -\dfrac{1}{2}(x - 1)$, so $y = -\dfrac{1}{2}x + \dfrac{3}{2}$.

m31-6-1-c.title: Tangent Lines and Linear Approximation, Part 3: Horizontal and Parallel Tangents

cues.prompt: At what point is the tangent to $y = x^{2} - 6x$ parallel to the line $y = 2x + 5$?

m31-6-1-d.title: Tangent Lines and Linear Approximation, Part 4: Linear Approximation

cues.prompt: Use a linear approximation at $a = 49$ to estimate $\sqrt{50}$.

m31-6-2.title: Increasing, Decreasing and Extreme Values, Part 1: Increasing and Decreasing

cues.prompt: On what interval is $f(x) = 8x - x^{2}$ increasing?
cues.working: $f'(x) = 8 - 2x$, which is positive when $x < 4$. So $f$ is increasing on $(-\infty, 4)$.

m31-6-2-b.title: Increasing, Decreasing and Extreme Values, Part 2: Critical Numbers

cues.prompt: Find the critical numbers of $f(x) = x^{3} - 12x + 5$.
cues.working: $f'(x) = 3x^{2} - 12 = 3(x^{2} - 4) = 3(x + 2)(x - 2)$, which is $0$ at $x = \pm 2$ and exists everywhere.

m31-6-2-c.title: Increasing, Decreasing and Extreme Values, Part 3: The First Derivative Test

cues.prompt: Which point is a local maximum of $f(x) = x^{3} - 12x + 5$?
cues.working: $f'(x) = 3(x + 2)(x - 2)$ changes from $+$ to $-$ at $x = -2$, so $f$ has a local maximum $f(-2) = -8 + 24 + 5 = 21$.

m31-6-2-d.title: Increasing, Decreasing and Extreme Values, Part 4: Absolute Extrema

cues.prompt: Find the absolute maximum value of $f(x) = x^{3} - 12x + 5$ on $[-3, 5]$.
cues.working: The critical numbers $-2$ and $2$ are in the interval. $f(-3) = 14$, $f(-2) = 21$, $f(2) = -11$ and $f(5) = 70$, so the absolute maximum is $70$, at $x = 5$.

m31-6-3.title: Concavity and Curve Sketching, Part 1: Concavity

cues.prompt: On what interval is $f(x) = x^{3} + 3x^{2} - 1$ concave up?
cues.working: $f'(x) = 3x^{2} + 6x$ and $f''(x) = 6x + 6$, which is positive when $x > -1$.

m31-6-3-b.title: Concavity and Curve Sketching, Part 2: Points of Inflection

cues.prompt: Find the point of inflection of $f(x) = x^{3} - 6x^{2} + 5$.
cues.working: $f''(x) = 6x - 12$ is $0$ at $x = 2$ and changes from $-$ to $+$ there. $f(2) = 8 - 24 + 5 = -11$.

m31-6-3-c.title: Concavity and Curve Sketching, Part 3: The Second Derivative Test

cues.prompt: $f(x) = x^{3} - 27x$ has critical numbers $-3$ and $3$. What does the second derivative test say?
choices: A local minimum at $-3$ and a local maximum at $3$
A local maximum at $-3$ and a local minimum at $3$
cues.working: $f''(x) = 6x$. $f''(-3) = -18 < 0$, a local maximum; $f''(3) = 18 > 0$, a local minimum.

m31-6-3-d.title: Concavity and Curve Sketching, Part 4: Curve Sketching

cues.prompt: Which describes $f(x) = x^{3} - 3x$ on the interval $(-1, 0)$?
cues.working: On $(-1, 0)$, $f'(x) = 3(x + 1)(x - 1) < 0$, so $f$ is decreasing, and $f''(x) = 6x < 0$, so $f$ is concave down.

m31-6-4.title: Motion Along a Line, Part 1: Velocity and Acceleration

cues.prompt: A particle has position $s(t) = 2t^{3} - 9t^{2} + 12t$ metres after $t$ seconds. Find its velocity and acceleration at $t = 3$.

m31-6-4-b.title: Motion Along a Line, Part 2: Direction of Motion

cues.prompt: A particle has position $s(t) = t^{2} - 8t + 3$ metres after $t$ seconds, for $t \ge 0$. When is it moving in the negative direction?
cues.working: $v(t) = 2t - 8$, which is negative when $t < 4$. So the particle moves in the negative direction for $0 \le t < 4$.

m31-6-4-c.title: Motion Along a Line, Part 3: Rising and Falling

cues.prompt: A ball thrown upward has height $h(t) = 2 + 24.5t - 4.9t^{2}$ metres after $t$ seconds. When is it highest, and how high is it then?

m31-6-4-d.title: Motion Along a Line, Part 4: Speeding Up or Slowing Down

cues.prompt: A particle has position $s(t) = t^{3} - 6t^{2} + 9t$ metres after $t$ seconds, for $t \ge 0$. When is it speeding up?
cues.working: $v(t) = 3(t - 1)(t - 3)$ and $a(t) = 6(t - 2)$. Both are negative on $(1, 2)$ and both positive on $(3, \infty)$.

m31-6-4-e.title: Motion Along a Line, Part 5: Displacement and Total Distance

cues.prompt: A particle has position $s(t) = t^{2} - 8t + 3$ metres after $t$ seconds. Find its displacement and the total distance it travels from $t = 0$ to $t = 6$.
cues.working: It turns around when $v(t) = 2t - 8 = 0$, at $t = 4$. $s(0) = 3$, $s(4) = -13$, $s(6) = -9$. Displacement: $-9 - 3 = -12$ m. Distance: $16 + 4 = 20$ m.

m31-7-1.title: Optimization, Part 1: The Strategy and a Fence by a River

cues.prompt: There is $240$ m of fencing for a rectangular field beside a straight river, with no fence along the river. What is the largest area it can enclose?

m31-7-1-b.title: Optimization, Part 2: Verifying a Maximum and the Largest Box

cues.prompt: An open box is folded from a $12$ cm by $12$ cm sheet by cutting a square of side $x$ cm from each corner. What size of square gives the largest volume?
cues.working: $V(x) = x(12 - 2x)^2$ for $0 < x < 6$, and $V'(x) = 12(x - 2)(x - 6)$. Only $x = 2$ is in the domain, and $V(2) = 2(8)(8) = 128$ cm³.

m31-7-1-c.title: Optimization, Part 3: Revenue and the Best Price

cues.prompt: A theatre sells $400$ tickets a night at \$20 each. For every \$1 increase in price, $10$ fewer tickets are sold. What ticket price brings in the most revenue?
cues.working: With $x$ increases of \$1, $R(x) = (20 + x)(400 - 10x) = 8{,}000 + 200x - 10x^2$. $R'(x) = 200 - 20x = 0$ gives $x = 10$: a price of \$30, with $300$ tickets sold, for \$9,000.

m31-7-1-d.title: Optimization, Part 4: The Can That Uses the Least Metal

cues.prompt: A closed cylindrical can must hold $1{,}000$ cm³. Which radius uses the least metal?
cues.working: $S(r) = 2\pi r^2 + \dfrac{2{,}000}{r}$, so $S'(r) = 4\pi r - \dfrac{2{,}000}{r^2} = 0$ gives $r^3 = \dfrac{500}{\pi}$ and $r \approx 5.42$ cm. The height is $2r \approx 10.84$ cm.

m31-7-1-e.title: Optimization, Part 5: Shortest Distance and Fastest Route

cues.prompt: Which point on the curve $y = \sqrt{x}$ is closest to the point $(5, 0)$?

m31-7-2.title: Related Rates, Part 1: Rates Linked by an Equation

cues.prompt: The radius of a circular oil spill grows at $2$ m/min. How fast is its area growing when the radius is $40$ m?
cues.working: $\dfrac{dA}{dt} = 2\pi r\,\dfrac{dr}{dt} = 2\pi(40)(2) = 160\pi \approx 503$ m²/min.

m31-7-2-b.title: Related Rates, Part 2: A Strategy and a Sliding Ladder

cues.prompt: A $13$ m ladder leans against a wall. Its foot slides away from the wall at $1$ m/s. How fast is the top sliding down when the foot is $5$ m from the wall?
cues.working: $x^2 + y^2 = 169$, so $2x\dfrac{dx}{dt} + 2y\dfrac{dy}{dt} = 0$. At $x = 5$, $y = 12$: $10 + 24\dfrac{dy}{dt} = 0$, so $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = -\dfrac{5}{12}$.

m31-7-2-c.title: Related Rates, Part 3: Similar Triangles, a Shadow and a Tank

cues.prompt: A conical tank, vertex down, has a top radius of $3$ m and a height of $6$ m. Water flows in at $4$ m³/min. How fast is the level rising when the water is $2$ m deep?
cues.working: $r = \dfrac{h}{2}$, so $V = \dfrac{\pi}{12}h^3$ and $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}h^2\dfrac{dh}{dt}$. Then $4 = \dfrac{\pi}{4}(4)\dfrac{dh}{dt}$, so $\dfrac{dh}{dt} = \dfrac{4}{\pi} \approx 1.27$ m/min.

m31-7-2-d.title: Related Rates, Part 4: Moving Cars and Changing Angles

cues.prompt: Car A is $6$ km north of an intersection, driving **toward** it at $50$ km/h. Car B is $8$ km east, driving away at $60$ km/h. How is the distance between them changing?
cues.working: $10\dfrac{dD}{dt} = 6(-50) + 8(60) = -300 + 480 = 180$, so $\dfrac{dD}{dt} = 18$ km/h, positive: the distance is increasing.

cues.prompt: Which function is an antiderivative of $3x^2$?
cues.working: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x^3 - 7\right) = 3x^2$. The others differentiate to $6$, $3x^2 + 3$ and $9x^2$.

m31-8-1-b.title: Antiderivatives, Part 2: The Power Rule in Reverse

cues.prompt: Find $\displaystyle\int (4x^3 - 6x + 2)\,dx$.
cues.working: $4\cdot\dfrac{x^4}{4} = x^4$, $-6\cdot\dfrac{x^2}{2} = -3x^2$ and $\int 2\,dx = 2x$. Check: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x^4 - 3x^2 + 2x\right) = 4x^3 - 6x + 2$.

cues.prompt: Find $\displaystyle\int \left(2\sin x + \frac{3}{x}\right)dx$ for $x > 0$.
cues.working: $\int 2\sin x\,dx = -2\cos x$ and $\int \dfrac{3}{x}\,dx = 3\ln x$. Check: $\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(-2\cos x + 3\ln x\right) = 2\sin x + \dfrac{3}{x}$.

m31-8-1-d.title: Antiderivatives, Part 4: Initial-Value Problems and Motion

cues.prompt: Find $f(x)$ given $f'(x) = 6x^2 + 2$ and $f(1) = 9$.

m31-8-2.title: Riemann Sums and Area, Part 1: Left and Right Sums

cues.prompt: Estimate the area under $f(x) = x^2$ on $[0, 4]$ with a **right** sum and $n = 4$.
cues.working: $\Delta x = 1$, and the right ends $1, 2, 3, 4$ give heights $1, 4, 9, 16$: $R_4 = 1(1 + 4 + 9 + 16) = 30$.

m31-8-2-b.title: Riemann Sums and Area, Part 2: Midpoints and the Definite Integral

cues.prompt: For $f(x) = 9 - x^2$ on $[0, 3]$, which statement is true?
choices: $L_n$ is an underestimate and $R_n$ an overestimate.
$L_n$ is an overestimate and $R_n$ an underestimate.
cues.working: On $[0, 3]$, $f$ decreases from $9$ to $0$, so each left end is the highest point of its subinterval and each right end the lowest.

m31-8-2-c.title: Riemann Sums and Area, Part 3: Sums from Data

cues.prompt: Water flows into a tank at $40$, $36$, $30$, $22$ and $12$ L/min, measured at $t = 0$, $5$, $10$, $15$ and $20$ min. Estimate the water added in the $20$ minutes with a **left** sum.
cues.working: $\Delta t = 5$, so $L_4 = 5(40 + 36 + 30 + 22) = 5(128) = 640$ L. The rate is decreasing, so this is an overestimate.

m31-8-3.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, Part 1: Net Area and the Theorem

cues.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_1^3 (2x + 1)\,dx$.

m31-8-3-b.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, Part 2: Evaluating and Properties

cues.prompt: Given $\int_0^5 f(x)\,dx = 8$ and $\int_0^2 f(x)\,dx = 3$, find $\int_5^2 f(x)\,dx$.
cues.working: $\int_2^5 f(x)\,dx = 8 - 3 = 5$, and reversing the limits changes the sign: $\int_5^2 f(x)\,dx = -5$.

m31-8-3-c.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, Part 3: Net Area, Total Area and Average Value

cues.prompt: Find the average value of $f(x) = 3x^2$ on $[0, 2]$.

m31-8-4.title: Integration by Substitution, Part 1: Reversing the Chain Rule

cues.prompt: Find $\displaystyle\int 2x(x^2 + 5)^3\,dx$.
cues.working: $u = x^2 + 5$ and $du = 2x\,dx$, so the integral is $\int u^3\,du = \dfrac{u^4}{4} + C = \dfrac{(x^2 + 5)^4}{4} + C$.

m31-8-4-b.title: Integration by Substitution, Part 2: Exponentials, Logarithms and Trigonometry

cues.prompt: Find $\displaystyle\int x^2 e^{x^3}\,dx$.
cues.working: $u = x^3$ and $du = 3x^2\,dx$, so $x^2\,dx = \tfrac{1}{3}\,du$ and the integral is $\tfrac{1}{3}\int e^u\,du = \tfrac{1}{3}e^{x^3} + C$.

m31-8-4-c.title: Integration by Substitution, Part 3: Definite Integrals and New Limits

cues.prompt: Evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^2 2x(x^2 + 1)^3\,dx$.
cues.working: $u = x^2 + 1$, $du = 2x\,dx$; the limits become $1$ and $5$. $\int_1^5 u^3\,du = \Big[\dfrac{u^4}{4}\Big]_1^5 = \dfrac{625 - 1}{4} = 156$.

m31-9-1.title: Area Between Curves, Part 1: Upper Curve Minus Lower Curve

cues.prompt: Find the area of the region between $y = x^2 + 4$ and $y = 2x$ from $x = 0$ to $x = 3$.

m31-9-1-b.title: Area Between Curves, Part 2: Finding the Limits

cues.prompt: Find the area of the region enclosed by $y = x^2$ and $y = x + 2$.
cues.working: $x^2 = x + 2$ gives $x = -1$ or $x = 2$, and the line is on top: $\int_{-1}^{2} (x + 2 - x^2)\,dx = \dfrac{10}{3} - \left(-\dfrac{7}{6}\right) = \dfrac{9}{2}$.

m31-9-1-c.title: Area Between Curves, Part 3: When the Curves Cross

cues.prompt: Find the total area enclosed by $y = x^3$ and $y = 4x$.
cues.working: $x^3 = 4x$ gives $x = -2, 0, 2$. $\int_0^2 (4x - x^3)\,dx = 8 - 4 = 4$, and the left region also has area $4$, so the total is $8$.

m31-9-1-d.title: Area Between Curves, Part 4: Integrating with Respect to y

cues.prompt: Find the area of the region enclosed by $x = y^2$ and $x = 4$.
cues.working: The curves meet at $y = -2$ and $y = 2$, and $x = 4$ is on the right: $\int_{-2}^{2} (4 - y^2)\,dy = \Big[4y - \dfrac{y^3}{3}\Big]_{-2}^{2} = \dfrac{16}{3} + \dfrac{16}{3} = \dfrac{32}{3}$.

m31-9-2.title: Volumes of Revolution, Part 1: Slicing into Discs

cues.prompt: The region under $y = x^2$ from $x = 0$ to $x = 1$ is rotated about the $x$-axis. Find the volume.
cues.working: $V = \pi\int_0^1 \left(x^2\right)^2 dx = \pi\int_0^1 x^4\,dx = \pi\Big[\dfrac{x^5}{5}\Big]_0^1 = \dfrac{\pi}{5}$.

m31-9-2-b.title: Volumes of Revolution, Part 2: A Cone and a Sphere

cues.prompt: The region under $y = 3x$ from $x = 0$ to $x = 2$ is rotated about the $x$-axis. Find the volume.
cues.working: $V = \pi\int_0^2 9x^2\,dx = \pi\Big[3x^3\Big]_0^2 = 24\pi$. Check: a cone of radius $6$ and height $2$ has $\tfrac{1}{3}\pi(36)(2) = 24\pi$.

m31-9-2-c.title: Volumes of Revolution, Part 3: Rotating About the y-Axis

cues.prompt: The first-quadrant region bounded by $y = x^2$, the $y$-axis and $y = 9$ is rotated about the $y$-axis. Find the volume.
cues.working: $x = \sqrt{y}$, so $V = \pi\int_0^9 y\,dy = \pi\Big[\dfrac{y^2}{2}\Big]_0^9 = \dfrac{81\pi}{2}$.

cues.prompt: The region between $y = 2x$ and $y = x^2$ is rotated about the $x$-axis. Find the volume.
cues.working: They meet at $x = 0$ and $x = 2$, with $R = 2x$ and $r = x^2$: $\pi\int_0^2 (4x^2 - x^4)\,dx = \pi\left(\dfrac{32}{3} - \dfrac{32}{5}\right) = \dfrac{64\pi}{15}$.

m103-1-1.title: Rates and Proportions, Part 1: Ratios, Rates and Unit Rates

cues.prompt: A courier drives $207\text{ km}$ in $2$ h $15$ min. What is the average speed?
cues.working: $15\text{ min} = 0.25\text{ h}$, so the time is $2.25\text{ h}$, and $207 \div 2.25 = 92\text{ km/h}$.

m103-1-1-b.title: Rates and Proportions, Part 2: Proportions on the Job

cues.prompt: A pickup uses $11.2\text{ L}$ per $100\text{ km}$, and gas costs \$1.52 per litre. What does gas cost for a $420\text{ km}$ trip?
cues.working: Litres: $\dfrac{11.2 \times 420}{100} = 47.04\text{ L}$. Cost: $47.04 \times 1.52 \approx 71.50$ dollars.

m103-1-2.title: Unit Price and Best Buys, Part 1: Finding a Unit Price

cues.prompt: A $1.5\text{ L}$ bottle of dish soap costs \$6.30. What is the unit price per $100\text{ mL}$?
cues.working: $1.5\text{ L} = 1500\text{ mL}$, which is $15$ groups of $100\text{ mL}$. Then $6.30 \div 15 = 0.42$ dollars.

m103-1-2-b.title: Unit Price and Best Buys, Part 2: The Best Buy

cues.prompt: Coffee costs \$7.49 for $340\text{ g}$ or \$19.99 for $925\text{ g}$. Which is the better buy?
choices: The $925\text{ g}$ bag, at about \$2.16 per $100\text{ g}$
The $340\text{ g}$ bag, at about \$2.20 per $100\text{ g}$
The $340\text{ g}$ bag, because it costs less
They cost the same per gram
cues.working: $7.49 \div 3.4 \approx 2.20$ and $19.99 \div 9.25 \approx 2.16$ dollars per $100\text{ g}$, so the big bag is slightly cheaper per unit.

m103-1-3.title: Markups, Sales and Taxes, Part 1: Percent Change, Markups and Discounts

cues.prompt: A drill is regularly \$120 and is on sale for $15\%$ off. What is the sale price?
cues.working: $15\%$ off means you pay $85\%$: $120 \times 0.85 = 102$ dollars.

m103-1-3-b.title: Markups, Sales and Taxes, Part 2: Two Discounts and Sales Tax

cues.prompt: A total of \$262.50 includes $5\%$ GST. What was the price before tax?
Suppose $1$ US dollar $= 1.35$ CAD. How many US dollars do you get for \$270 CAD?
cues.working: The rate starts with US dollars, but you have CAD, so divide: $270 \div 1.35 = 200$.

m103-1-4-b.title: Currency Exchange, Part 2: Buy Rates, Sell Rates and Fees

cues.prompt: Using the table (bank buys euros at $1.4870$ CAD, sells at $1.5810$ CAD), what does it cost to buy €250?
cues.working: You are buying euros, so the bank is selling: $250 \times 1.5810 = 395.25$ dollars.

m103-2-1.title: Hourly Wages and Overtime, Part 1: Gross Pay and Timecards

cues.prompt: A shift runs from 9:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. with a 30-minute unpaid break, at \$16.80 per hour. What is the gross pay?
cues.working: 9:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. is 7 h 30 min. Minus 30 min: 7 h. Then $7 \times 16.80 = 117.60$ dollars.

m103-2-1-b.title: Hourly Wages and Overtime, Part 2: Overtime

cues.prompt: Lee earns \$20.00 per hour, with time-and-a-half for hours over 40 in a week. Lee worked 44 hours. What is the gross pay?
cues.working: $40 \times 20 = 800$, and $4 \times 30 = 120$, so the gross pay is $920$ dollars.

m103-2-2.title: Salary, Commission and Piecework, Part 1: Salary and Commission

cues.prompt: A salary of \$46,800 a year is paid weekly. How much is each pay cheque?
cues.working: Weekly means 52 pays: $46{,}800 \div 52 = 900$ dollars.

m103-2-2-b.title: Salary, Commission and Piecework, Part 2: Graduated Commission and Piecework

cues.prompt: A salesperson earns 2% on the first \$20,000 of sales and 6% on sales above \$20,000. Sales were \$35,000. What is the commission?
cues.working: $0.02 \times 20{,}000 = 400$, and $0.06 \times 15{,}000 = 900$, so the commission is $1300$ dollars.

m103-2-3.title: Comparing Pay and Contracts, Part 1: Job Offers and Break-Even

cues.prompt: Job A pays \$900 a week. Job B pays \$300 a week plus 8% of sales. What weekly sales make them pay the same?

m103-2-3-b.title: Comparing Pay and Contracts, Part 2: Working on Contract

cues.prompt: A carpenter wants \$48 per hour. A deck will take 30 hours and the lumber costs \$1,250. What should the bid be?

m103-2-4.title: Deductions and Net Pay, Part 1: From Gross to Net

cues.prompt: Gross pay is \$800. Income tax is 15% of gross pay above \$500. What is the income tax?

m103-2-4-b.title: Deductions and Net Pay, Part 2: Take-Home Pay and Working Backward

cues.prompt: A job pays \$1,500 a month plus 5% commission. What monthly sales give earnings of \$2,700?

m103-3-1.title: SI Units, Part 1: Prefixes and Converting

cues.prompt: A truck carries $4.2$ tonnes of gravel. How many kilograms is that?
cues.working: $1\text{ t} = 1000\text{ kg}$. Kilograms are smaller, so multiply: $4.2 \times 1000 = 4200\text{ kg}$.

m103-3-1-b.title: SI Units, Part 2: Mixed Units, Volume and Capacity

cues.prompt: A cattle trough is $2.4\text{ m}$ long, $60\text{ cm}$ wide and $50\text{ cm}$ deep. How many litres does it hold?
A pipe is $103\text{ in}$ long. What is this in feet and inches?
cues.working: $103 \div 12 = 8$ remainder $7$, since $8 \times 12 = 96$. So $103\text{ in} = 8\text{ ft } 7\text{ in}$.

m103-3-2-b.title: Imperial Units, Part 2: Mass and Capacity

cues.prompt: A recipe needs $5$ US quarts of stock. How many cups is that?
cues.working: $1\text{ qt} = 2\text{ pt} = 4$ cups, so $5\text{ qt} = 5 \times 4 = 20$ cups.

m103-3-3.title: Converting Between Systems, Part 1: Conversion Factors

cues.prompt: A trip is $240\text{ km}$. About how many miles is it? Use $1\text{ mi} \approx 1.609\text{ km}$.
cues.working: Miles are bigger than kilometres, so divide: $240 \div 1.609 \approx 149\text{ mi}$.

m103-3-3-b.title: Converting Between Systems, Part 2: Imperial to SI and Estimates

cues.prompt: A board is $8\text{ ft}$ long. How long is it in centimetres? Use $1\text{ ft} = 30.48\text{ cm}$.
cues.working: Centimetres are smaller, so multiply: $8 \times 30.48 = 243.84\text{ cm}$.

cues.prompt: A washer lies along a ruler from the $3.7\text{ cm}$ mark to the $5.2\text{ cm}$ mark. How wide is it, in millimetres?

m103-4-1-b.title: Rulers and Tape Measures, Part 2: Imperial Rulers

cues.prompt: A bar ends $10$ sixteenths past the $2$ in mark. How long is it?
cues.working: $\tfrac{10}{16} = \tfrac58$, so the bar is $2\tfrac58$ in long.

m103-4-2.title: Working with Fractional Measurements, Part 1: Adding and Subtracting Inches

cues.prompt: Find $5\tfrac38 - 1\tfrac{11}{16}$ in.

m103-4-2-b.title: Working with Fractional Measurements, Part 2: Saw Kerf, Feet and Inches

cues.prompt: A wall is $11\text{ ft } 3\text{ in}$ long. A cabinet run takes $6\text{ ft } 8\text{ in}$. How much wall is left?
cues.working: $11\text{ ft } 3\text{ in} = 10\text{ ft } 15\text{ in}$, and $10\text{ ft } 15\text{ in} - 6\text{ ft } 8\text{ in} = 4\text{ ft } 7\text{ in}$.

cues.prompt: A rectangular window is $1.2\text{ m}$ wide and $90\text{ cm}$ tall. How much trim goes around it?

m103-4-3-b.title: Perimeter and Circumference, Part 2: Circumference and Working Backward

cues.prompt: A round table has a radius of $0.6\text{ m}$. How much edging goes around it, to the nearest hundredth of a metre?
cues.working: $C = 2\pi r = 2\pi(0.6) \approx 3.77\text{ m}$.

m103-4-4.title: Cutting and Buying Material, Part 1: How Many Pieces?

cues.prompt: How many $60\text{ cm}$ pieces can be cut from a $4\text{ m}$ rod, ignoring the kerf?
cues.working: $400 \div 60 \approx 6.67$. Round down: $6$ whole pieces, with $40\text{ cm}$ left over.

m103-4-4-b.title: Cutting and Buying Material, Part 2: Buying by Length

cues.prompt: Fencing costs \$8.75 per linear metre. A rectangular yard is $20\text{ m}$ by $15\text{ m}$, with a $1\text{ m}$ gate that needs no fencing. What does the fencing cost, before tax?
cues.working: $P = 2(20 + 15) = 70\text{ m}$, minus the gate: $69\text{ m}$. Then $69 \times 8.75 = 603.75$ dollars.

m103-5-1.title: Area of Common Shapes, Part 1: Rectangles, Triangles and Trapezoids

cues.prompt: A triangular sail has a base of $12\text{ m}$ and a perpendicular height of $5\text{ m}$. Its slanted side is $7\text{ m}$. What is its area?
cues.working: $A = \tfrac12 bh = \tfrac12 \times 12 \times 5 = 30\text{ m}^2$.

m103-5-1-b.title: Area of Common Shapes, Part 2: Circles and Working Backward

cues.prompt: A circular patio has an area of $50\text{ m}^2$. What is its radius, to the nearest tenth of a metre?
cues.working: $r^2 = \dfrac{50}{\pi} \approx 15.92$, so $r = \sqrt{15.92} \approx 4.0\text{ m}$.

m103-5-2.title: Composite and Irregular Areas, Part 1: Composite Shapes

cues.prompt: A garage wall is $20\text{ ft}$ by $9\text{ ft}$, with a door $16\text{ ft}$ by $7\text{ ft}$. What area of wall is left to paint?

m103-5-2-b.title: Composite and Irregular Areas, Part 2: Irregular Shapes

cues.prompt: On a grid of $1\text{ m}^2$ squares, a pond covers $20$ full squares and $12$ partly covered squares. Estimate its area.
cues.working: Full squares plus half of the partly covered ones: $20 + 12 \div 2 = 26\text{ m}^2$.

m103-5-3.title: Surface Area, Part 1: Boxes and the Faces You Need

cues.prompt: A closed box is $10\text{ cm}$ by $8\text{ cm}$ by $5\text{ cm}$. What is its surface area?
A closed can has a radius of $4\text{ cm}$ and a height of $10\text{ cm}$. What is its surface area, to the nearest square centimetre?

m103-5-4.title: Area Units and Material Costs, Part 1: Square Units

cues.prompt: A patio is $36\text{ ft}^2$. How many square yards is that?
cues.working: $1\text{ yd}^2 = 9\text{ ft}^2$, and square yards are bigger, so divide: $36 \div 9 = 4\text{ yd}^2$.

m103-5-4-b.title: Area Units and Material Costs, Part 2: How Much to Buy

cues.prompt: A floor is $200\text{ ft}^2$. Add 10% for waste. Each box of tile covers $15\text{ ft}^2$. How many boxes are needed?
cues.working: $200 \times 1.10 = 220\text{ ft}^2$, and $220 \div 15 \approx 14.67$. Round up: $15$ boxes.

cues.prompt: What kind of angle measures $181^\circ$?
cues.working: $181^\circ$ is more than $180^\circ$, so it is reflex. Only exactly $180^\circ$ is a straight angle.

cues.prompt: Three angles meet at a point. Two of them measure $150^\circ$ and $95^\circ$. What does the third angle measure?
cues.working: Angles around a point add to $360^\circ$: $360^\circ - (150^\circ + 95^\circ) = 360^\circ - 245^\circ = 115^\circ$.

m103-6-2.title: Angle Relationships, Part 1: Complementary and Supplementary

cues.prompt: An angle measures $38^\circ$. What is its complement?
cues.working: Complementary angles add to $90^\circ$: $90^\circ - 38^\circ = 52^\circ$.

m103-6-2-b.title: Angle Relationships, Part 2: Vertically Opposite Angles and Bisectors

cues.prompt: Two vertically opposite angles measure $(4x + 5)^\circ$ and $(2x + 45)^\circ$. What is $x$?
cues.working: They are equal: $4x + 5 = 2x + 45$, so $2x = 40$ and $x = 20$. Each angle is $85^\circ$.

m103-6-3.title: Parallel Lines, Part 1: Transversals and Angle Pairs

cues.prompt: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. Which pair of angles **add to** $180^\circ$?
cues.working: Co-interior angles (same side, between the lines) add to $180^\circ$. The other pairs are equal.

m103-6-3-b.title: Parallel Lines, Part 2: Finding Angles and Testing for Parallel

cues.prompt: A transversal crosses two parallel lines. A pair of alternate interior angles measure $(2x + 30)^\circ$ and $(4x - 10)^\circ$. What is $x$?
cues.working: Alternate interior angles are equal: $2x + 30 = 4x - 10$, so $40 = 2x$ and $x = 20$. Each angle is $70^\circ$.

m103-6-4.title: Spatial Puzzles, Part 1: Counting Squares and Rectangles

cues.prompt: How many squares, of all sizes, are in a $4 \times 4$ grid?
cues.working: $16 + 9 + 4 + 1 = 30$ squares: sixteen $1 \times 1$, nine $2 \times 2$, four $3 \times 3$ and one $4 \times 4$.

m103-6-4-b.title: Spatial Puzzles, Part 2: Painted Cubes and Dice

cues.prompt: A $3\text{ cm}$ cube is painted on all six faces, then cut into $1\text{ cm}$ cubes. How many small cubes have exactly **two** painted faces?
cues.working: Each of the $12$ edges has $3 - 2 = 1$ middle cube: $12 \times 1 = 12$.

m103-7-1.title: The Pythagorean Theorem, Part 1: Finding the Hypotenuse

cues.prompt: A right triangle has legs of $9\text{ cm}$ and $12\text{ cm}$. How long is the hypotenuse?

m103-7-1-b.title: The Pythagorean Theorem, Part 2: Finding a Leg and Checking for Square

cues.prompt: The hypotenuse of a right triangle is $10\text{ m}$ and one leg is $6\text{ m}$. How long is the other leg?

m103-7-2.title: Pythagorean Problems, Part 1: Ladders and Rafters

cues.prompt: A $13\text{ ft}$ ladder leans against a wall with its foot $5\text{ ft}$ from the wall. How high up the wall does it reach?
cues.working: The ladder is the hypotenuse: $h^2 = 13^2 - 5^2 = 169 - 25 = 144$, so $h = 12\text{ ft}$.

m103-7-2-b.title: Pythagorean Problems, Part 2: Diagonals and Two-Step Problems

cues.prompt: A TV screen is $32\text{ in}$ wide and $18\text{ in}$ tall. What size is it, to the nearest inch?

m103-7-3.title: Similar Polygons, Part 1: Same Shape, Different Size

cues.prompt: Rectangle P is $10\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$. Which rectangle is similar to P?
cues.working: $\tfrac{15}{10} = 1.5$ and $\tfrac{6}{4} = 1.5$: the ratios are equal. For B, $\tfrac{12}{10} = 1.2$ but $\tfrac{6}{4} = 1.5$.

m103-7-3-b.title: Similar Polygons, Part 2: The Scale Factor

chapters.title: The photo that will not fit

cues.prompt: A logo $20\text{ cm}$ wide is printed $5\text{ cm}$ wide on a business card. What is the scale factor?
cues.working: $k = \dfrac{\text{new}}{\text{original}} = \dfrac{5}{20} = 0.25$, a reduction.

m103-7-4.title: Similar Figures, Part 1: Missing Sides and Shadows

cues.prompt: A $2\text{ m}$ post casts a $3\text{ m}$ shadow. At the same time, a tree casts a $12\text{ m}$ shadow. How tall is the tree?
cues.working: $\dfrac{h}{12} = \dfrac{2}{3}$, so $h = 12 \times \dfrac{2}{3} = 8\text{ m}$.

cues.prompt: On a $1:100$ plan, a room is $4.5\text{ cm}$ long. How long is the real room?

m103-8-1.title: The Tangent Ratio, Part 1: Naming the Sides

cues.prompt: In a right triangle, the side opposite $\theta$ is $9$, the side adjacent to $\theta$ is $12$ and the hypotenuse is $15$. What is $\tan\theta$?
cues.working: $\tan\theta = \dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}} = \dfrac{9}{12} = 0.75$.

m103-8-1-b.title: The Tangent Ratio, Part 2: Finding Sides and Angles

cues.prompt: A ramp rises $0.8\text{ m}$ over a horizontal run of $6\text{ m}$. What angle does it make with the ground, to the nearest tenth of a degree?
cues.working: $\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{0.8}{6}\right) \approx 7.6^\circ$.

m103-8-2.title: Sine and Cosine, Part 1: Choosing the Ratio

cues.prompt: A $4\text{ m}$ ladder makes a $70^\circ$ angle with the ground. You want the distance from the wall to its foot. Which ratio should you use?
cues.working: The ladder is the hypotenuse, and the distance along the ground touches the $70^\circ$ angle, so it is adjacent. Adjacent and hypotenuse: CAH, cosine.

m103-8-2-b.title: Sine and Cosine, Part 2: Finding Sides and Angles

cues.prompt: A $4\text{ m}$ ladder makes a $70^\circ$ angle with the ground. How far is its foot from the wall, to the nearest tenth of a metre?
cues.working: The distance is adjacent and the ladder is the hypotenuse: $d = 4\cos 70^\circ \approx 1.4\text{ m}$.

m103-8-3.title: Trigonometry on the Job, Part 1: Elevation and Depression

cues.prompt: From the top of a $20\text{ m}$ cliff, a boat is at an angle of depression of $30^\circ$. How far is the boat from the base of the cliff?
cues.working: The angle at the boat is also $30^\circ$. The height is opposite and the distance is adjacent: $d = \dfrac{20}{\tan 30^\circ} \approx 34.6\text{ m}$.

m103-8-3-b.title: Trigonometry on the Job, Part 2: Roofs, Ramps and Ladders

cues.prompt: A $10\text{ m}$ ladder is set at $75^\circ$ to the ground. How high up the wall does it reach, to the nearest tenth of a metre?
cues.working: The height is opposite and the ladder is the hypotenuse: $h = 10 \sin 75^\circ \approx 9.7\text{ m}$.

m104-1-1.title: Place Value, Part 1: Reading and Writing Numbers

cues.prompt: What is the value of the $8$ in $38{,}516$?
cues.working: The $8$ is in the thousands place, so it is worth $8 \times 1{,}000 = 8{,}000$.

m104-1-1-b.title: Place Value, Part 2: Comparing and Rounding

cues.prompt: Round $7{,}952$ to the nearest hundred.
cues.working: The hundreds digit is $9$ and the digit to its right is $5$, so round up. One more hundred than $7{,}900$ is $8{,}000$.

m104-1-2.title: The Four Operations, Part 1: Choosing the Operation

cues.prompt: Each shelf holds $15$ boxes. How many shelves do you need for $100$ boxes?
cues.working: $100 \div 15 = 6$ remainder $10$. The $10$ extra boxes still need a shelf, so round up to $7$.

m104-1-2-b.title: The Four Operations, Part 2: The Order of Operations

cues.prompt: Find the value of $18 - 4 \times 3$.
cues.working: Multiply first: $4 \times 3 = 12$. Then subtract: $18 - 12 = 6$.

m104-1-3.title: Estimating, Part 1: Is the Answer Reasonable?

cues.prompt: A school orders $29$ boxes of paper at \$41 a box. About how much does it spend?
cues.working: Round: $29 \approx 30$ and $41 \approx 40$. Then $30 \times 40 = 1{,}200$.

cues.prompt: A store gets $12$ cases of $24$ cans. It sells $150$ cans. How many cans are left?
cues.working: $12 \times 24 = 288$ cans, and $288 - 150 = 138$ cans left.

m104-2-1.title: Fractions, Part 1: Parts of a Whole

cues.prompt: Fill in the missing number: $\dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{?}{12}$
cues.working: The bottom changed from $3$ to $12$, which is $\times 4$. Do the same to the top: $2 \times 4 = 8$.

m104-2-1-b.title: Fractions, Part 2: Lowest Terms and Comparing

cues.prompt: Which is bigger: $\dfrac{3}{4}$ inch or $\dfrac{11}{16}$ inch?
cues.working: $\dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{12}{16}$, and $12 > 11$, so $\dfrac{3}{4}$ inch is bigger.

cues.prompt: A crew of $30$ workers is told that $\dfrac{2}{5}$ of them work the night shift. How many work nights?
cues.working: One part: $30 \div 5 = 6$. Two parts: $2 \times 6 = 12$.

m104-2-3.title: Adding and Subtracting Fractions, Part 1: Common Denominators

cues.prompt: Find $\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{3}$.
cues.working: Common denominator $6$: $\dfrac{3}{6} + \dfrac{2}{6} = \dfrac{5}{6}$.

m104-2-3-b.title: Adding and Subtracting Fractions, Part 2: Mixed Numbers

cues.prompt: Find $4\dfrac{1}{8} - 1\dfrac{5}{8}$.
cues.working: Regroup: $4\tfrac{1}{8} = 3\tfrac{9}{8}$. Then $3\tfrac{9}{8} - 1\tfrac{5}{8} = 2\tfrac{4}{8} = 2\tfrac{1}{2}$.

m104-3-1.title: Decimals and Money, Part 1: Place Value, Adding and Subtracting

cues.working: Write $5.6$ as $5.60$, line up the points, and subtract: $5.60 - 2.35 = 3.25$.

m104-3-1-b.title: Decimals and Money, Part 2: Multiplying, Dividing and Making Change

cues.prompt: A total is \$7.38. You pay with a \$10 bill by card. What is your change?
cues.working: Card payments are not rounded: $10.00 - 7.38 = 2.62$.

cues.prompt: Write $\dfrac{2}{5}$ as a percent.

m104-3-3.title: Percents of Money, Part 1: Percent of an Amount and Tips

cues.prompt: A haircut costs \$32. You leave a $20\%$ tip. How much is the tip?

m104-3-3-b.title: Percents of Money, Part 2: Discounts and GST

cues.prompt: A shirt costs \$40 and is $25\%$ off. Then $5\%$ GST is added. What is the total?
cues.working: Discount: $0.25 \times 40 = 10$, so the sale price is \$30. GST: $0.05 \times 30 = 1.50$. Total: \$31.50.

cues.prompt: Which temperature is the coldest?
cues.working: $-12$ is farthest left on a number line, so it is the least, and the coldest.

cues.prompt: The temperature is $-9^\circ\text{C}$ at night and $4^\circ\text{C}$ the next afternoon. By how many degrees did it rise?
cues.working: Rise = higher − lower: $4 - (-9) = 4 + 9 = 13$ degrees.

m104-5-1.title: Patterns, Part 1: Tables and Extending Patterns

cues.prompt: What is the next term? $3, \; 6, \; 12, \; 24, \; \ldots$
cues.working: The jumps are $3, 6, 12$, so it is not adding. Each term doubles: $24 \times 2 = 48$.

cues.prompt: A pattern goes $7, \; 11, \; 15, \; 19, \; \ldots$ for $n = 1, 2, 3, 4$. Which rule fits?
cues.working: The jump is $4$, so the rule starts with $4n$. When $n = 1$, $4n = 4$, and $7 - 4 = 3$. So $y = 4n + 3$.

m104-5-2.title: Expressions and Formulas, Part 1: Variables and Expressions

cues.prompt: A gym charges a \$25 sign-up fee plus \$30 per month. Which expression gives the cost for $m$ months?
cues.working: The monthly part changes with $m$: $30m$. The sign-up fee is paid once: $+\,25$.

m104-5-2-b.title: Expressions and Formulas, Part 2: Using Formulas

cues.prompt: Use $C = 5 + 3k$ to find the cost $C$ when $k = 8$.
cues.working: Substitute and multiply first: $C = 5 + 3(8) = 5 + 24 = 29$.

cues.prompt: Solve $5x + 3 = 38$.
cues.working: Subtract $3$: $5x = 35$. Divide by $5$: $x = 7$. Check: $5 \times 7 + 3 = 38$.

cues.prompt: On Jordan’s pay graph, the line goes from \$0 at 0 hours to \$160 at 8 hours. How much does Jordan earn for 3 hours?
cues.working: The pay goes up \$20 each hour: $3 \times 20 = 60$.

m104-6-1.title: Metric Units, Part 1: Choosing and Estimating

cues.prompt: Which is the best estimate for the height of a classroom door?
cues.working: A door is a little taller than an adult, about two big steps: $2\text{ m}$.

cues.prompt: A bag of flour has a mass of $2.5\text{ kg}$. How many grams is that?
cues.working: Kilograms to grams is big to small, so multiply: $2.5 \times 1000 = 2500\text{ g}$.

cues.prompt: On a ruler with $16$ spaces in each inch, a screw ends $6$ spaces past the $1$-inch mark. How long is it?
cues.working: $1\tfrac{6}{16}$ in, and $\tfrac{6}{16} = \tfrac{3}{8}$, so the screw is $1\tfrac{3}{8}$ in long.

m104-6-3.title: Time and Temperature, Part 1: Elapsed Time

cues.prompt: A shift runs from 9:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. How long is it?
cues.working: 9:30 to 10:00 is 30 min, 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. is 7 h. Total: 7 h 30 min.

m104-6-3-b.title: Time and Temperature, Part 2: Reading Temperatures

cues.prompt: It was $3^\circ\text{C}$ at noon and $-8^\circ\text{C}$ at midnight. How many degrees did the temperature drop?
cues.working: From $3$ down to $0$ is $3$ degrees, and from $0$ down to $-8$ is $8$ more: $3 + 8 = 11$.

cues.prompt: A square patio has sides of $3.5\text{ m}$. What is its perimeter?
cues.working: A square has four equal sides: $P = 4 \times 3.5 = 14\text{ m}$.

cues.prompt: A round pool has a radius of $4\text{ m}$. How long is the fence around it, to the nearest tenth?
cues.working: $d = 2 \times 4 = 8\text{ m}$, and $C = \pi \times 8 \approx 25.1\text{ m}$.

cues.prompt: A triangular sail has a base of $5\text{ m}$ and a height of $8\text{ m}$. What is its area?
cues.working: $A = \tfrac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 8 = 20\text{ m}^2$.

cues.prompt: Flooring costs \$30 per square metre. A room is $5\text{ m}$ by $4\text{ m}$. What does the flooring cost?
cues.working: Area: $5 \times 4 = 20\text{ m}^2$. Cost: $20 \times 30 = 600$ dollars.

cues.prompt: A storage bin is $50\text{ cm}$ long, $40\text{ cm}$ wide and $30\text{ cm}$ high. What is its volume?
cues.working: $V = 50 \times 40 \times 30 = 60\,000\text{ cm}^3$.

cues.prompt: A water tank is $100\text{ cm}$ by $50\text{ cm}$ by $40\text{ cm}$. How many litres does it hold?

m104-8-1.title: Angles and Shapes, Part 1: Types of Angles

cues.prompt: Two angles make a straight line. One is $125^\circ$. What is the other?
cues.working: Angles on a straight line add to $180^\circ$: $180 - 125 = 55^\circ$.

m104-8-1-b.title: Angles and Shapes, Part 2: Triangles and Quadrilaterals

cues.prompt: A triangle has sides of $5\text{ cm}$, $7\text{ cm}$ and $9\text{ cm}$. Name it by its sides.
cues.working: No two sides are equal, so the triangle is scalene.

m104-8-2.title: 3-D Objects, Part 1: Faces, Edges and Vertices

cues.prompt: A square pyramid has a square base and $4$ triangle faces. How many edges does it have?
cues.working: $4$ edges around the base and $4$ going up to the top: $4 + 4 = 8$ edges.

cues.prompt: In a top view, one column has a stack of $4$ boxes with a stack of $1$ box behind it. How many boxes high is that column in the front view?
cues.working: The front view shows the tallest stack in the column: $4$ boxes.

m104-8-3.title: Symmetry and Transformations, Part 1: Lines of Symmetry

cues.prompt: A triangular road sign has $3$ equal sides and nothing written on it. How many lines of symmetry does it have?
cues.working: A fold from each corner to the middle of the opposite side makes the halves match: $3$ lines.

m104-8-3-b.title: Symmetry and Transformations, Part 2: Slides, Flips and Turns

cues.prompt: A game piece at $(3, 1)$ slides $2$ units left and $4$ units up. Where is its image?
cues.working: Left subtracts from $x$: $3 - 2 = 1$. Up adds to $y$: $1 + 4 = 5$. The image is $(1, 5)$.

m104-9-1.title: Data and Graphs, Part 1: Tallies and Bar Graphs

cues.prompt: The grid lines on a bar graph go up by $4$. A bar stops halfway between the lines for $12$ and $16$. What value does it show?
cues.working: Halfway between $12$ and $16$ is $14$.

m104-9-1-b.title: Data and Graphs, Part 2: Circle Graphs and Fair Surveys

cues.prompt: A school asks whether to build a new sports field. Which sample is fair?
choices: $30$ students picked at random from the school list
cues.working: Picking at random from the whole school gives every student the same chance to be asked.

cues.prompt: Find the median of $9$, $4$, $7$, $12$ and $5$.
cues.working: In order: $4,\ 5,\ 7,\ 9,\ 12$. The middle value is $7$.

m104-9-2-b.title: Averages, Part 2: Mode, Range and Outliers

cues.prompt: Find the range of $14$, $9$, $21$, $9$ and $17$.
cues.working: Highest $21$, lowest $9$: $21 - 9 = 12$.

m104-9-3.title: Probability, Part 1: How Likely Is It?

cues.prompt: A box has $4$ cherry, $7$ lemon and $9$ lime candies. What is the probability of picking lemon?
cues.working: Total: $4 + 7 + 9 = 20$. Favourable: $7$. $P(\text{lemon}) = \dfrac{7}{20}$.

m104-9-3-b.title: Probability, Part 2: Percents and Comparing Chances

cues.prompt: Bag C has $8$ marbles and $2$ are red. Bag D has $12$ marbles and $4$ are red. Which bag gives the better chance of red?
cues.working: Bag C: $\dfrac{2}{8} = 25\%$. Bag D: $\dfrac{4}{12} \approx 33.3\%$. Bag D is better.

m201-1-1.title: Arithmetic Sequences, Part 1: The General Term

cues.prompt: Find $t_{25}$ for the arithmetic sequence $7,\ 10,\ 13,\ \ldots$

m201-1-1-b.title: Arithmetic Sequences, Part 2: Missing Terms and Positions

cues.prompt: In an arithmetic sequence, $t_3 = 11$ and $t_8 = 31$. Find the common difference $d$.

m201-1-2.title: Arithmetic Series, Part 1: Reverse and Add

cues.prompt: Find the sum of the first $10$ terms of $2 + 5 + 8 + \cdots$

m201-1-2-b.title: Arithmetic Series, Part 2: Finding n, and Problems

chapters.title: When the last term is given

cues.prompt: Find the sum of $4 + 9 + 14 + \cdots + 99$.

m201-1-3.title: Geometric Sequences, Part 1: The Common Ratio

cues.prompt: Find $t_6$ for the geometric sequence $5,\ 15,\ 45,\ \ldots$

m201-1-3-b.title: Geometric Sequences, Part 2: Missing Terms, Growth and Decay

cues.prompt: A town of $8000$ people grows by $5\%$ each year. Which expression gives its population after $6$ years?
cues.working: Growth by $5\%$ multiplies by $r = 1.05$ each year, and the starting value is at time $0$, so after $6$ years: $8000(1.05)^6$.

m201-1-4.title: Geometric Series, Part 1: The Sum Formula

cues.prompt: Find the sum of the first $6$ terms of $4 + 12 + 36 + \cdots$

m201-1-4-b.title: Geometric Series, Part 2: Last Terms, Salaries and Bounces

cues.prompt: Find the sum of $1 + 2 + 4 + \cdots + 512$.

m201-1-5.title: Infinite Geometric Series, Part 1: Converging to a Sum

cues.prompt: Which infinite geometric series converges?
cues.working: Its ratio is $\frac{1}{3}$, and $|r| < 1$. The others have $r = 2$, $r = -1$ and $r = 1.5$.

m201-1-5-b.title: Infinite Geometric Series, Part 2: Using the Sum

cues.prompt: Find the sum of $12 - 6 + 3 - \cdots$
cues.working: $r = -\frac{1}{2}$, and $S_\infty = \dfrac{12}{1 - \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{12}{1.5} = 8$.

m201-2-1.title: Angles in Standard Position, Part 1: Reference Angles

cues.prompt: Find the reference angle of $\theta = 250^\circ$.
cues.working: $250^\circ$ is in quadrant III, so $\theta_R = 250^\circ - 180^\circ = 70^\circ$.

m201-2-1-b.title: Angles in Standard Position, Part 2: Special Triangles

cues.prompt: What is the exact value of $\cos 60^\circ$?
cues.working: In the $30^\circ$–$60^\circ$–$90^\circ$ triangle, the side adjacent to $60^\circ$ is $1$ and the hypotenuse is $2$: $\cos 60^\circ = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

m201-2-1-c.title: Angles in Standard Position, Part 3: Exact Values in Every Quadrant

cues.prompt: What is the exact value of $\sin 300^\circ$?
cues.working: Quadrant IV: $\theta_R = 60^\circ$ and $y < 0$, so $\sin 300^\circ = -\sin 60^\circ = -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$.

m201-2-2.title: Trigonometric Ratios of Any Angle, Part 1: Points and CAST

cues.prompt: $P(-6, -8)$ is on the terminal arm of $\theta$. What is $\sin\theta$?

m201-2-2-b.title: Trigonometric Ratios of Any Angle, Part 2: Solving for Angles

cues.working: $\theta_R = 60^\circ$, and cosine is positive in quadrants I and IV: $60^\circ$ and $360^\circ - 60^\circ = 300^\circ$.

m201-2-3.title: The Sine Law, Part 1: Finding Sides

cues.prompt: In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A = 40^\circ$, $\angle C = 75^\circ$ and $a = 8$ cm. Which equation gives $c$?
cues.working: $\dfrac{c}{\sin 75^\circ} = \dfrac{8}{\sin 40^\circ}$, so $c = \dfrac{8\sin 75^\circ}{\sin 40^\circ} \approx 12.0$ cm.

m201-2-3-b.title: The Sine Law, Part 2: Finding Angles

cues.prompt: $\sin B = 0.5$ and $\angle B$ is obtuse. What is $\angle B$?
cues.working: $\sin^{-1}(0.5) = 30^\circ$, and the obtuse angle with the same sine is $180^\circ - 30^\circ = 150^\circ$.

m201-2-4.title: The Ambiguous Case, Part 1: How Many Triangles?

cues.prompt: $\angle A = 40^\circ$, $b = 10$ cm and $a = 8$ cm. How many triangles are possible?
cues.working: $h = 10\sin 40^\circ \approx 6.43$, and $6.43 < 8 < 10$, so there are two triangles.

m201-2-4-b.title: The Ambiguous Case, Part 2: Solving Both Triangles

cues.prompt: In an ambiguous case, $\sin B \approx 0.7660$. What are the two possible measures of $\angle B$?
cues.working: $\sin^{-1}(0.7660) \approx 50^\circ$, and its supplement is $180^\circ - 50^\circ = 130^\circ$.

m201-2-5.title: The Cosine Law, Part 1: Finding a Side

cues.prompt: In $\triangle ABC$, $b = 5$, $c = 7$ and $\angle A = 60^\circ$. Find $a$.

m201-2-5-b.title: The Cosine Law, Part 2: Finding Angles and Choosing a Law

cues.prompt: In $\triangle ABC$, $a = 8$, $b = 5$ and $c = 6$. Which expression gives $\cos A$?
cues.working: The side opposite $\angle A$, $a = 8$, is the one subtracted: $\cos A = \dfrac{25 + 36 - 64}{60} = -0.05$, so $\angle A \approx 92.9^\circ$.

m201-2-5-c.title: The Cosine Law, Part 3: Two-Step Problems

cues.prompt: A triangle has two sides of $10$ m and $14$ m, with a $35^\circ$ angle between them. Which law finds the third side?
cues.working: Two sides and the contained angle (SAS): there is no complete side–angle pair, so use the cosine law.

m201-3-1.title: Quadratic Functions in Vertex Form, Part 1: Transforming y = x²

cues.prompt: How is the graph of $y = (x + 5)^2 - 2$ related to the graph of $y = x^2$?
cues.working: $x + 5 = x - (-5)$, so $p = -5$: $5$ units left. $q = -2$: $2$ units down.

m201-3-1-b.title: Quadratic Functions in Vertex Form, Part 2: Reading the Features

cues.prompt: What is the vertex of $y = 3(x - 2)^2 + 7$, and is it a maximum or a minimum?
cues.working: $p = 2$ and $q = 7$, so the vertex is $(2, 7)$. $a = 3 > 0$, so the parabola opens up and $7$ is the minimum value.

m201-3-1-c.title: Quadratic Functions in Vertex Form, Part 3: Domain, Range and Models

cues.prompt: What is the range of $y = -(x - 1)^2 + 4$?
cues.working: The vertex is $(1, 4)$ and $a = -1 < 0$, so the parabola opens down and $4$ is the maximum value: $y \le 4$.

cues.working: The product $P = x(20 - x)$ has zeros $0$ and $20$, so the vertex is at $x = 10$. Both numbers are $10$, and $P = 100$.

m201-3-4-b.title: Solving Optimization Problems, Part 2: Area and Revenue

cues.prompt: In this example, a store sells $200$ shirts a week at \$10 each. For every \$1 increase in price, $10$ fewer shirts are sold. What price maximizes revenue?
cues.working: The zeros of $R(x) = (10 + x)(200 - 10x)$ are $x = -10$ and $x = 20$, so $x = 5$ and the price is \$15.

m201-4-2.title: Solving Quadratic Equations, Part 1: Roots and Graphs

cues.working: The graph of $y = x^2 + 2$ has its vertex at $(0, 2)$, above the $x$-axis, and opens up, so it never meets the axis.

m201-4-3-c.title: Completing the Square and the Quadratic Formula, Part 3: Using the Formula

m201-4-4.title: The Discriminant and Applications, Part 1: The Discriminant

cues.prompt: How many real roots does $3x^2 + 2x + 1 = 0$ have?
cues.working: $b^2 - 4ac = 2^2 - 4(3)(1) = 4 - 12 = -8 < 0$, so there are no real roots.

m201-4-4-b.title: The Discriminant and Applications, Part 2: Unknown Coefficients and Problems

cues.prompt: For which values of $k$ does $x^2 + 4x + k = 0$ have no real roots?
cues.working: No real roots: $b^2 - 4ac = 16 - 4k < 0$, so $16 < 4k$ and $k > 4$.

m201-5-1.title: Working with Radicals, Part 1: Simplest Form

cues.prompt: Write $\sqrt{72}$ in simplest form.
cues.working: The largest perfect square dividing $72$ is $36$: $\sqrt{72} = \sqrt{36}\,\sqrt{2} = 6\sqrt{2}$.

m201-5-1-b.title: Working with Radicals, Part 2: Variables and Comparing

cues.prompt: Which is greater, $5\sqrt{2}$ or $3\sqrt{6}$?
choices: It cannot be decided without a calculator.
cues.working: $5\sqrt{2} = \sqrt{50}$ and $3\sqrt{6} = \sqrt{54}$. Since $54 > 50$, $3\sqrt{6}$ is greater.

m201-5-1-c.title: Working with Radicals, Part 3: Adding and Subtracting

cues.prompt: Simplify $\sqrt{75} - \sqrt{12}$.
cues.working: $\sqrt{75} = 5\sqrt{3}$ and $\sqrt{12} = 2\sqrt{3}$, so $\sqrt{75} - \sqrt{12} = 3\sqrt{3}$.

m201-5-2.title: Multiplying and Dividing Radicals, Part 1: Multiplying

cues.prompt: Expand $\left(1 + \sqrt{5}\right)^2$.
cues.working: $\left(1 + \sqrt{5}\right)^2 = 1 + \sqrt{5} + \sqrt{5} + 5 = 6 + 2\sqrt{5}$.

m201-5-2-b.title: Multiplying and Dividing Radicals, Part 2: Conjugates and Rationalizing

cues.prompt: Rationalize $\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{6}}$.
cues.working: $\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{6}} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{6}} = \dfrac{3\sqrt{6}}{6} = \dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{2}$.

m201-5-2-c.title: Multiplying and Dividing Radicals, Part 3: Binomial Denominators

cues.prompt: Rationalize $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{3} - 1}$.
cues.working: Multiply by $\dfrac{\sqrt{3} + 1}{\sqrt{3} + 1}$. The denominator is $3 - 1 = 2$, so the result is $\dfrac{2\left(\sqrt{3} + 1\right)}{2} = \sqrt{3} + 1$.

m201-5-3.title: Radical Equations, Part 1: Restrictions and Squaring

cues.prompt: State the restriction on $x$ in $\sqrt{10 - 5x}$.
cues.working: $10 - 5x \ge 0$, so $-5x \ge -10$. Dividing by $-5$ reverses the inequality: $x \le 2$.

cues.prompt: Solve $\sqrt{x + 1} = x - 1$.
cues.working: Squaring gives $x + 1 = x^2 - 2x + 1$, so $x^2 - 3x = 0$ and $x = 0$ or $x = 3$. Check: $x = 0$ gives $1 \ne -1$, so it is extraneous; $x = 3$ gives $2 = 2$.

m201-5-3-c.title: Radical Equations, Part 3: Two Radicals and Models

cues.prompt: Solve $\sqrt{x + 5} = \sqrt{x} + 1$.
cues.working: Squaring gives $x + 5 = x + 2\sqrt{x} + 1$, so $2\sqrt{x} = 4$, $\sqrt{x} = 2$ and $x = 4$. Check: $\sqrt{9} = 3 = \sqrt{4} + 1$.

cues.prompt: What are the non-permissible values of $\dfrac{x - 3}{x^2 - 9x + 14}$?
$\dfrac{(x + 3)(x - 4)}{(x - 4)(x + 1)}$ simplifies to $\dfrac{x + 3}{x + 1}$. What are the restrictions?
cues.working: The restrictions come from the original denominator, $(x - 4)(x + 1)$: $x \ne 4$ and $x \ne -1$.

chapters.title: A trinomial over a difference of squares

cues.prompt: Simplify $\dfrac{x^2 - 9}{x^2 + 5x + 6}$.
cues.working: $\dfrac{(x - 3)(x + 3)}{(x + 2)(x + 3)} = \dfrac{x - 3}{x + 2}$, with $x \ne -2,\ -3$ from the original denominator.

m201-6-2.title: Multiplying and Dividing Rational Expressions, Part 1: Multiplying

cues.prompt: Simplify $\dfrac{x + 1}{x - 2} \times \dfrac{x^2 - 4}{3x + 3}$.
cues.working: $\dfrac{x + 1}{x - 2} \times \dfrac{(x - 2)(x + 2)}{3(x + 1)} = \dfrac{x + 2}{3}$. The denominators give $x \ne 2$ and $x \ne -1$.

m201-6-2-b.title: Multiplying and Dividing Rational Expressions, Part 2: Dividing

m201-6-3.title: Adding and Subtracting Rational Expressions, Part 1: Common Denominators

cues.prompt: Simplify $\dfrac{2}{x} + \dfrac{3}{x^2}$.
cues.working: The LCD is $x^2$: $\dfrac{2x}{x^2} + \dfrac{3}{x^2} = \dfrac{2x + 3}{x^2}$, with $x \ne 0$.

m201-6-3-b.title: Adding and Subtracting Rational Expressions, Part 2: Factoring Denominators

m201-6-4.title: Rational Equations, Part 1: Multiplying by the LCD

cues.prompt: Solve $\dfrac{5}{x} - \dfrac{1}{3x} = \dfrac{2}{3}$.
cues.working: Multiply every term by $3x$: $15 - 1 = 2x$, so $x = 7$. Check: $\tfrac{5}{7} - \tfrac{1}{21} = \tfrac{14}{21} = \tfrac{2}{3}$.

cues.prompt: Solve $\dfrac{1}{x - 2} + \dfrac{x}{x + 2} = \dfrac{4}{x^2 - 4}$.
cues.working: Multiply by $(x - 2)(x + 2)$: $(x + 2) + x(x - 2) = 4$, so $x^2 - x - 2 = 0$ and $x = 2$ or $x = -1$. Reject $x = 2$, which is non-permissible.

m201-6-4-c.title: Rational Equations, Part 3: Work and Travel Problems

cues.prompt: Jo can paint a fence in $3$ h, and Sam in $6$ h. How long will they take together?
cues.working: $\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{2}{6} + \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}$, so $\dfrac{1}{t} = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $t = 2$.

m201-7-4-b.title: Reciprocal Functions, Part 2: Features and Sketching

cues.prompt: What are the invariant points of $y = \dfrac{1}{x - 5}$?
cues.working: $x - 5 = 1$ gives $x = 6$, the point $(6, 1)$; $x - 5 = -1$ gives $x = 4$, the point $(4, -1)$.

cues.prompt: How many vertical asymptotes does $y = \dfrac{1}{x^2 + 4}$ have?
cues.working: $x^2 + 4 \ge 4$, so it is never $0$. There are no vertical asymptotes, and the graph has one branch.

m201-8-1.title: Solving Systems Graphically, Part 1: A Line and a Parabola

cues.prompt: Which point is a solution of the system $y = x^2$ and $y = x + 2$?
cues.working: $(2, 4)$ makes both equations true: $2^2 = 4$ and $2 + 2 = 4$.

m201-8-1-b.title: Solving Systems Graphically, Part 2: Two Parabolas

cues.prompt: How many solutions does the system $y = x^2 + 2$ and $y = x^2 - 3$ have?
cues.working: Both parabolas have $a = 1$ and the axis $x = 0$: one is the other translated $5$ units down, so they never meet.

m201-8-2-b.title: Solving Systems Algebraically, Part 2: Tangents and Elimination

cues.prompt: Solve the system $y = x^2 + 1$ and $y = 2x^2 - 3$.
Two positive numbers differ by $3$, and their product is $40$. What are they?
cues.working: $x(x + 3) = 40$, so $x^2 + 3x - 40 = (x + 8)(x - 5) = 0$. Both numbers are positive, so $x = 5$, and the numbers are $5$ and $8$.

m201-9-1.title: Linear Inequalities in Two Variables, Part 1: Graphing

cues.prompt: Is $(4, 1)$ a solution of $2x - 3y > 6$?
choices: Only if the boundary is solid
cues.working: $2(4) - 3(1) = 5$, and $5 > 6$ is false, so $(4, 1)$ is not a solution.

m201-9-1-b.title: Linear Inequalities in Two Variables, Part 2: Checking and Modelling

cues.prompt: In this example, a bake sale sells muffins at \$2 and cookies at \$1, and must take in more than \$80. Which inequality fits, for $m$ muffins and $c$ cookies?
cues.working: The money taken in is $2m + c$, and "more than" means $>$.

m201-9-2.title: Quadratic Inequalities in One Variable, Part 1: Test Intervals

cues.prompt: Solve $x^2 - 4x < 0$.
cues.working: $x(x - 4) = 0$ at $x = 0$ and $x = 4$. Testing $x = 2$ gives $4 - 8 = -4 < 0$, so the middle interval works, and $<$ leaves out the roots.

m201-9-2-b.title: Quadratic Inequalities in One Variable, Part 2: Sign Diagrams

cues.prompt: Solve $(x - 1)(x + 5) \ge 0$.
cues.working: The roots are $-5$ and $1$. Both factors are negative when $x < -5$, and both positive when $x > 1$, so the product is positive outside the roots; $\ge$ includes them.

m201-9-2-c.title: Quadratic Inequalities in One Variable, Part 3: Rearranging and Problems

cues.prompt: Solve $x^2 \ge 16$.
cues.working: $x^2 - 16 = (x - 4)(x + 4) \ge 0$, which is true outside the roots: $x \le -4$ or $x \ge 4$.

m201-9-3.title: Quadratic Inequalities in Two Variables, Part 1: Graphing the Region

cues.prompt: Is $(2, 5)$ a solution of $y \le x^2 + 1$?
choices: Yes: it is on the boundary, which is included.
No: it is on the boundary.
Yes: it is above the parabola.
No: it is below the parabola.
cues.working: $2^2 + 1 = 5$, and $5 \le 5$ is true. The point is on the solid boundary, so it is a solution.

m201-9-3-b.title: Quadratic Inequalities in Two Variables, Part 2: Reading Graphs and Models

cues.prompt: Which inequality describes the region on and above the solid parabola $y = x^2 - 4$?
cues.working: A solid boundary is included, so the sign is $\ge$ or $\le$; shading above means $y \ge$.

m202-1-1.title: Making Conjectures: Inductive Reasoning, Part 1: Conjectures

cues.prompt: Mina notices that $2 \times 3 = 6$, $4 \times 5 = 20$ and $6 \times 7 = 42$. Which conjecture fits all three?
choices: The product is a multiple of 6.
cues.working: $6$, $20$ and $42$ are all even. $20$ is not a multiple of 6, $6$ and $42$ do not end in 0, and $6$ is not greater than 10.

m202-1-1-b.title: Making Conjectures: Inductive Reasoning, Part 2: Patterns

cues.prompt: Figure 1 has $5$ tiles, Figure 2 has $8$ and Figure 3 has $11$. Which rule fits?
cues.working: $3(1) + 2 = 5$, $3(2) + 2 = 8$ and $3(3) + 2 = 11$. The other rules fit Figure 1 at most.

cues.prompt: Conjecture: "If a number is a multiple of 3, then it is odd." Which number is a counterexample?
cues.working: $12$ is a multiple of 3, so it meets the condition, but it is even, so the conclusion is false. $7$ is not a multiple of 3.

cues.prompt: Conjecture: "The sum of two numbers is always greater than each of the numbers." Which pair is a counterexample?
cues.working: $3 + (-1) = 2$, which is not greater than $3$. The other pairs all support the conjecture.

m202-1-3.title: Proving Conjectures: Deductive Reasoning, Part 1: Deductive Proof

cues.prompt: To prove that the sum of any even integer and any odd integer is odd, how should you write the two integers?
cues.working: $2m$ is any even integer and $2n + 1$ is any odd integer. Then $2m + 2n + 1 = 2(m + n) + 1$, which is odd. B only covers consecutive integers.

m202-1-3-b.title: Proving Conjectures: Deductive Reasoning, Part 2: Number Tricks and Invalid Proofs

cues.prompt: A student writes: $(-5)^2 = 25$ and $5^2 = 25$, so $(-5)^2 = 5^2$. Taking the square root of both sides, $-5 = 5$. What is the error?
choices: Taking the square root drops the negative root.
cues.working: If $x^2 = 5^2$, then $x = 5$ or $x = -5$. Taking only the positive root ignores the negative one.

m202-1-4.title: Reasoning to Solve Problems and Puzzles, Part 1: Number and Logic Puzzles

cues.prompt: Kai is thinking of a two-digit multiple of $8$. The sum of its digits is $10$. What is the number?
cues.working: Two-digit multiples of 8: $16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 72, 80, 88, 96$. Only $64$ has a digit sum of $10$. The others are not multiples of 8.

m202-1-4-b.title: Reasoning to Solve Problems and Puzzles, Part 2: Games and Winning Strategies

cues.prompt: In the same game, there are $22$ counters and you go first. How many should you take?
cues.working: The nearest multiple of 4 below 22 is 20, so take $22 - 20 = 2$. Then leave 16, 12, 8, 4 and 0.

m202-1-4-c.title: Reasoning to Solve Problems and Puzzles, Part 3: Spatial Puzzles

cues.prompt: How many squares, of all sizes, are in a $4 \times 4$ grid?
cues.working: $16$ squares that are $1 \times 1$, $9$ that are $2 \times 2$, $4$ that are $3 \times 3$ and $1$ that is $4 \times 4$: $16 + 9 + 4 + 1 = 30$.

m202-2-1.title: Angles Formed by Parallel Lines, Part 1: Transversals and Angle Pairs

cues.prompt: Two angles are between two parallel lines, on the same side of a transversal. What kind of pair are they, and how are they related?
cues.working: Between the lines is interior, and on the same side of the transversal is same-side. With parallel lines, same-side interior angles are supplementary.

m202-2-1-b.title: Angles Formed by Parallel Lines, Part 2: Finding Angles with Reasons

cues.prompt: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. A pair of same-side interior angles measure $(2x + 20)^\circ$ and $(3x + 10)^\circ$. What is $x$?
cues.working: Same-side interior angles add to $180^\circ$: $5x + 30 = 180$, so $5x = 150$ and $x = 30$. The angles are $80^\circ$ and $100^\circ$. Setting them equal gives the wrong answer, $10$.

m202-2-1-c.title: Angles Formed by Parallel Lines, Part 3: Extra Lines and Proving Lines Parallel

cues.prompt: A transversal crosses two lines. A pair of same-side interior angles measure $95^\circ$ and $85^\circ$. Are the lines parallel?
choices: No: the angles are not equal.
cues.working: $95^\circ + 85^\circ = 180^\circ$, so the same-side interior angles are supplementary, and the lines are parallel.

m202-2-2.title: Angles in Triangles, Part 1: The Angle Sum

cues.prompt: A right triangle has one angle of $34^\circ$. What is its third angle?
cues.working: The angles are $90^\circ$, $34^\circ$ and $x$: $x = 180^\circ - 90^\circ - 34^\circ = 56^\circ$.

m202-2-2-b.title: Angles in Triangles, Part 2: Isosceles Triangles and Algebra

cues.prompt: In an isosceles triangle, the angle between the two equal sides is $52^\circ$. What is each of the other two angles?
cues.working: The other two angles are equal: $2x + 52^\circ = 180^\circ$, so $2x = 128^\circ$ and $x = 64^\circ$.

m202-2-2-c.title: Angles in Triangles, Part 3: Exterior Angles

cues.prompt: An exterior angle of a triangle measures $120^\circ$. One of its non-adjacent interior angles measures $45^\circ$. What is the other one?
cues.working: The exterior angle equals the sum of the non-adjacent interior angles: $45^\circ + x = 120^\circ$, so $x = 75^\circ$.

m202-2-3.title: Angle Properties of Polygons, Part 1: The Interior Angle Sum

cues.prompt: What is the sum of the interior angles of a convex heptagon (7 sides)?
cues.working: $S = 180^\circ(7 - 2) = 180^\circ(5) = 900^\circ$. $1260^\circ$ is $180^\circ \times 7$, which forgets the 2.

m202-2-3-b.title: Angle Properties of Polygons, Part 2: Regular Polygons

cues.prompt: Each interior angle of a regular polygon measures $140^\circ$. How many sides does it have?
cues.working: Each exterior angle is $180^\circ - 140^\circ = 40^\circ$, so $n = 360^\circ \div 40^\circ = 9$.

m202-2-3-c.title: Angle Properties of Polygons, Part 3: Solving Polygon Problems

cues.prompt: Five angles of a convex hexagon measure $130^\circ$, $110^\circ$, $125^\circ$, $140^\circ$ and $115^\circ$. What is the sixth angle?
cues.working: A hexagon’s angles add to $180^\circ(4) = 720^\circ$. The five known angles add to $620^\circ$, so the sixth is $720^\circ - 620^\circ = 100^\circ$.

cues.prompt: $\triangle JKL \cong \triangle RST$. Which side is equal to $KL$?
cues.working: $K$ matches $S$ and $L$ matches $T$ (second and third letters), so $KL = ST$.

m202-2-4-b.title: Congruent Triangles, Part 2: SSS, SAS and ASA

chapters.title: Using an angle that is not included

cues.prompt: In $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle DEF$, $AB = DE$, $BC = EF$ and $\angle C = \angle F$. Which condition proves them congruent?
cues.working: The angle between $AB$ and $BC$ is $\angle B$, not $\angle C$. So the angle is not included, and SSA does not prove congruence.

cues.prompt: $\triangle PQS$ and $\triangle RQS$ share side $QS$. $PQ = RQ$ and $\angle PQS = \angle RQS$. Which condition proves them congruent?
cues.working: $PQ = RQ$ (given), $\angle PQS = \angle RQS$ (given) and $QS = QS$ (common side). The angle at $Q$ is between $PQ$ and $QS$, so it is included: SAS.

m202-3-1.title: The Sine Law, Part 1: Matching Pairs and the Proof

cues.prompt: In $\triangle PQR$, which side and angle form a matching pair?
cues.working: Side $q$ is named after the angle opposite it, $\angle Q$. Side $PQ$ is $r$, which is opposite $\angle R$.

m202-3-1-b.title: The Sine Law, Part 2: Finding a Side

cues.prompt: In acute $\triangle DEF$, $\angle D = 50^\circ$, $\angle E = 60^\circ$ and $d = 10$ m. Determine $e$, to the nearest tenth of a metre.
cues.working: $\dfrac{e}{\sin 60^\circ} = \dfrac{10}{\sin 50^\circ}$, so $e = \dfrac{10\sin 60^\circ}{\sin 50^\circ} \approx 11.3$ m. B flips the sines.

m202-3-1-c.title: The Sine Law, Part 3: Finding an Angle

cues.prompt: In acute $\triangle ABC$, $a = 9$ cm, $b = 7$ cm and $\angle A = 64^\circ$. Determine $\angle B$, to the nearest degree.
cues.working: $\sin B = \dfrac{7\sin 64^\circ}{9} \approx 0.6991$, so $\angle B = \sin^{-1}(0.6991) \approx 44^\circ$. It is smaller than $64^\circ$, because $b < a$.

m202-3-2.title: The Cosine Law, Part 1: When the Sine Law Cannot Start

cues.prompt: Which set of information gives no matching pair, so the cosine law is needed to start?
cues.working: $\angle C$ is the contained angle of $a$ and $b$, and $c$ is unknown: SAS. B and C contain the pair $a$ and $\angle A$, and in D the angle sum gives $\angle C$ to pair with $c$.

m202-3-2-b.title: The Cosine Law, Part 2: Finding a Side

chapters.title: Two sides and the contained angle

cues.prompt: In acute $\triangle ABC$, $a = 8$ cm, $b = 10$ cm and $\angle C = 50^\circ$. Determine $c$, to the nearest tenth of a centimetre.
cues.working: $c^2 = 64 + 100 - 160\cos 50^\circ \approx 61.15$, so $c \approx 7.8$ cm. D forgets the square root, and C subtracts before multiplying.

m202-3-2-c.title: The Cosine Law, Part 3: Finding an Angle and Using Both Laws

cues.prompt: An acute triangle has sides $6$ cm, $8$ cm and $9$ cm. Determine its largest angle, to the nearest degree.
cues.working: The largest angle is opposite $9$: $\cos\theta = \dfrac{6^2 + 8^2 - 9^2}{2(6)(8)} = \dfrac{19}{96} \approx 0.1979$, so $\theta \approx 79^\circ$.

m202-3-3.title: Solving Problems with the Sine and Cosine Laws, Part 1: Choosing a Method

cues.prompt: In $\triangle KLM$, you know $k = 8$, $\angle K = 40^\circ$ and $\angle L = 75^\circ$. You want $l$. Which method should you use?
cues.working: $k$ and $\angle K$ are a matching pair, and $l$ is opposite the known $\angle L$, so $\dfrac{l}{\sin 75^\circ} = \dfrac{8}{\sin 40^\circ}$.

m202-3-3-b.title: Solving Problems with the Sine and Cosine Laws, Part 2: Surveying and Navigation

cues.prompt: From a point, it is $300$ m to one end of a pond and $250$ m to the other end, with $48^\circ$ between the lines of sight. How long is the pond, to the nearest metre?
cues.working: $d^2 = 300^2 + 250^2 - 2(300)(250)\cos 48^\circ \approx 52\,130$, so $d \approx 228$ m. D forgets the square root, and C subtracts before multiplying.

m202-3-3-c.title: Solving Problems with the Sine and Cosine Laws, Part 3: Problems with Two Steps

cues.prompt: Two points are $500$ m apart, with a balloon between them. Its angles of elevation are $58^\circ$ and $50^\circ$. How high is the balloon, to the nearest metre?
cues.working: The top angle is $72^\circ$. The slanted side from the $58^\circ$ point is $\dfrac{500\sin 50^\circ}{\sin 72^\circ} \approx 402.73$, so $h \approx 402.73\sin 58^\circ \approx 342$ m.

m202-4-1.title: Mixed and Entire Radicals, Part 1: Simplifying Radicals

cues.prompt: Write $\sqrt{98}$ as a mixed radical in simplest form.
cues.working: $98 = 49 \times 2$, so $\sqrt{98} = \sqrt{49} \times \sqrt{2} = 7\sqrt{2}$.

m202-4-1-b.title: Mixed and Entire Radicals, Part 2: Mixed to Entire

cues.prompt: Write $6\sqrt{2}$ as an entire radical.
cues.working: $6 = \sqrt{36}$, so $6\sqrt{2} = \sqrt{36} \times \sqrt{2} = \sqrt{72}$. B multiplies $6 \times 2$ without squaring the $6$.

m202-4-1-c.title: Mixed and Entire Radicals, Part 3: Ordering Radicals and Exact Lengths

cues.prompt: Order $3\sqrt{2}$, $2\sqrt{5}$ and $4$ from least to greatest.

m202-4-2.title: Adding, Subtracting and Multiplying Radicals, Part 1: Like Radicals

cues.prompt: Simplify $\sqrt{50} + \sqrt{8}$.
cues.working: $\sqrt{50} = 5\sqrt{2}$ and $\sqrt{8} = 2\sqrt{2}$, so the sum is $7\sqrt{2}$. B adds the radicands.

m202-4-2-b.title: Adding, Subtracting and Multiplying Radicals, Part 2: Perimeters and Products

cues.prompt: Simplify $\left(3\sqrt{2}\right)\left(4\sqrt{6}\right)$.
cues.working: $(3 \times 4)\sqrt{2 \times 6} = 12\sqrt{12} = 12 \times 2\sqrt{3} = 24\sqrt{3}$. B is correct but not in simplest form.

m202-4-2-c.title: Adding, Subtracting and Multiplying Radicals, Part 3: The Distributive Property

cues.prompt: Expand and simplify $\left(3 + \sqrt{2}\right)\left(1 + \sqrt{2}\right)$.
cues.working: $3 + 3\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{2} + 2 = 5 + 4\sqrt{2}$. B keeps only two of the four products.

cues.prompt: Simplify $\dfrac{20\sqrt{21}}{5\sqrt{3}}$.
cues.working: $\dfrac{20}{5} = 4$ and $\dfrac{21}{3} = 7$, so the quotient is $4\sqrt{7}$.

m202-4-3-b.title: Dividing Radicals, Part 2: Rationalizing the Denominator

cues.prompt: Rationalize the denominator: $\dfrac{6}{\sqrt{2}}$.
cues.working: $\dfrac{6}{\sqrt{2}} \times \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{6\sqrt{2}}{2} = 3\sqrt{2}$. B multiplies only the denominator.

m202-4-3-c.title: Dividing Radicals, Part 3: Two Terms in the Numerator

cues.prompt: Simplify $\dfrac{8 + \sqrt{12}}{\sqrt{2}}$ so that the denominator has no radical.
cues.working: $\dfrac{8\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{24}}{2} = \dfrac{8\sqrt{2} + 2\sqrt{6}}{2} = 4\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{6}$.

m202-4-4.title: Radical Equations, Part 1: Isolate, Then Undo

cues.prompt: Solve $3\sqrt{x + 2} - 1 = 11$.
Solve $\sqrt{2x + 3} + 5 = 2$.
cues.working: $\sqrt{2x + 3} = -3$, and a square root is never negative. Squaring gives $x = 3$, but $\sqrt{9} + 5 = 8 \ne 2$, so it is extraneous.

m202-4-4-c.title: Radical Equations, Part 3: Radical Equations in Context

chapters.title: The volume of an exercise ball

cues.prompt: In this example, the speed of a wave in water $d$ m deep is modelled by $s = \sqrt{9.8d}$ m/s. A wave travels at $50$ m/s. How deep is the water, to the nearest tenth of a metre?
cues.working: Square both sides: $2500 = 9.8d$, so $d = \dfrac{2500}{9.8} \approx 255.1$ m. D divides $50$ by $9.8$ without squaring.

cues.prompt: Find the population standard deviation of $4,\ 6,\ 8,\ 10,\ 12$.
cues.working: $\mu = 8$. The squared deviations are $16, 4, 0, 4, 16$, which add to $40$. $\sigma = \sqrt{\dfrac{40}{5}} = \sqrt{8} \approx 2.83$.

m202-5-1-b.title: Standard Deviation, Part 2: Calculators and Frequency Tables

cues.prompt: The value $1$ occurs twice, $2$ occurs four times and $3$ occurs twice. Find the population standard deviation.
Two archers: Ana’s scores have a mean of $8.2$ and $\sigma = 0.6$. Ben’s have a mean of $8.5$ and $\sigma = 1.9$. Who is more consistent?
choices: Ana: her standard deviation is smaller.
Ben: his standard deviation is larger.
cues.working: Consistency is about spread. Ana’s scores are typically $0.6$ points from her mean, and Ben’s about $1.9$. Ben scores more on average, but Ana is more consistent.

m202-5-2.title: The Normal Distribution, Part 1: The Normal Curve

cues.prompt: Exam marks are normally distributed with a mean of $72\%$. What percent of students scored above the mean?
cues.working: The normal curve is symmetric about the mean, so half of the data is above it.

m202-5-2-b.title: The Normal Distribution, Part 2: The 68–95–99.7 Rule

cues.prompt: The heights have $\mu = 168$ cm and $\sigma = 8$ cm. What percent of the students are shorter than $152$ cm?
cues.working: $152$ is $2\sigma$ below the mean. Below it: $2.35\% + 0.15\% = 2.5\%$. B counts both tails.

m202-5-2-c.title: The Normal Distribution, Part 3: Using the Normal Model

cues.prompt: Test scores are normally distributed, and about $68\%$ of them are between $85$ and $115$. Find the mean and the standard deviation.
cues.working: The mean is halfway: $100$. $68\%$ is within $1\sigma$ each side, so the interval is $2\sigma = 30$ wide, and $\sigma = 15$.

m202-5-3.title: Z-Scores, Part 1: Standard Deviations from the Mean

chapters.title: From a z-score to a value

cues.prompt: Battery lives have $\mu = 50$ h and $\sigma = 4$ h. What is the z-score of a battery that lasts $44$ h?
cues.working: $z = \dfrac{44 - 50}{4} = \dfrac{-6}{4} = -1.5$. It is below the mean, so the z-score is negative.

cues.prompt: Which result is better compared with the others: $82$ on a test with $\mu = 70$, $\sigma = 6$, or $90$ on a test with $\mu = 80$, $\sigma = 8$?
cues.working: $\dfrac{82 - 70}{6} = 2$ and $\dfrac{90 - 80}{8} = 1.25$. The $82$ is further above its mean.

m202-5-3-c.title: Z-Scores, Part 3: Areas under the Normal Curve

cues.prompt: For the heights ($\mu = 168$ cm, $\sigma = 8$ cm), what percent of students are taller than $172$ cm? The table gives $0.6915$ for $z = 0.50$.
cues.working: $z = \dfrac{172 - 168}{8} = 0.5$, and the area to the left is $0.6915$. Taller is to the right: $1 - 0.6915 = 0.3085$, about $30.9\%$.

m202-5-3-d.title: Z-Scores, Part 4: From a Percent to a Value

cues.prompt: For the heights ($\mu = 168$ cm, $\sigma = 8$ cm), what height separates the shortest $20\%$? The closest table area to $0.20$ is $0.2005$, at $z = -0.84$.
cues.working: The shortest $20\%$ is to the left, so use $z = -0.84$: $x = 168 + (-0.84)(8) = 161.28$, about $161.3$ cm. B is the tallest $20\%$.

m202-5-4.title: Confidence Intervals, Part 1: Margin of Error

cues.prompt: A report says that between $27\%$ and $35\%$ of students walk to school. What were the survey result and the margin of error?
cues.working: Midpoint: $\dfrac{27 + 35}{2} = 31$. Half the width: $\dfrac{35 - 27}{2} = 4$. B uses the whole width.

m202-5-4-b.title: Confidence Intervals, Part 2: Confidence Level and Sample Size

chapters.title: What changes the margin of error

cues.prompt: A pollster wants a smaller margin of error while keeping a $95\%$ confidence level. What should change?
choices: Report the result to more decimal places.
cues.working: A larger random sample gives a smaller margin of error. B widens the interval, and C makes it wider too.

cues.prompt: A poll finds $52\%$ support for a new bylaw, accurate to within $3$ percentage points, 19 times out of 20. Can supporters be confident of a majority?
choices: No: the interval includes values below $50\%$.
Yes: the margin of error is small.
cues.working: The interval is $49\%$ to $55\%$. It includes values below $50\%$, so a majority is not certain at this confidence level.

m202-6-1.title: Quadratic Functions and Their Graphs, Part 1: Parabolas

cues.prompt: A parabola has zeros $-5$ and $1$. What is its axis of symmetry?
cues.working: The axis of symmetry is halfway between the zeros: $\dfrac{-5 + 1}{2} = -2$, so it is the vertical line $x = -2$.

m202-6-1-b.title: Quadratic Functions and Their Graphs, Part 2: Maximum, Minimum, Domain and Range

cues.prompt: A parabola opens up and has its vertex at $(3, -2)$. What is its range?
cues.working: It opens up, so the vertex is the lowest point, and its $y$-coordinate, $-2$, is the minimum value: $y \ge -2$.

m202-6-1-c.title: Quadratic Functions and Their Graphs, Part 3: Parabolas in Context

cues.prompt: A rocket’s height has its vertex at $(4, 80)$, in seconds and metres, and it lands after $8$ s. Which statement is true?
choices: It is in the air for $4$ s.
cues.working: The vertex gives the time ($4$ s) and the maximum height ($80$ m). It is in the air for $8$ s, and the range is $0 \le h \le 80$.

m202-6-2.title: Axis of Symmetry and Optimization, Part 1: Finding the Axis of Symmetry

chapters.title: Any two points at the same height

cues.prompt: The points $(-3, 8)$ and $(5, 8)$ are on a parabola. What is its axis of symmetry?
cues.working: Both points have $y = 8$, so the axis is halfway between them: $x = \dfrac{-3 + 5}{2} = 1$.

m202-6-2-b.title: Axis of Symmetry and Optimization, Part 2: Maximum and Minimum Values

cues.prompt: Find the vertex of $y = x^2 - 6x + 2$.
cues.working: $x = -\dfrac{-6}{2(1)} = 3$, and $y = 9 - 18 + 2 = -7$. B uses the wrong sign for $b$.

m202-6-2-c.title: Axis of Symmetry and Optimization, Part 3: Optimization Problems

cues.prompt: A farmer has $80$ m of fencing for a rectangular pen against a barn wall, so only three sides need fencing. What is the greatest possible area?
cues.working: $A = x(80 - 2x) = -2x^2 + 80x$. The vertex is at $x = 20$, so the pen is $20$ m by $40$ m, and $A = 800\ \text{m}^2$. D gives $x$, not the area.

m202-6-3.title: Quadratic Functions in Factored Form, Part 1: Reading the Zeros

cues.prompt: What are the zeros of $y = -3(x + 4)(x - 2)$?
cues.working: $x + 4 = 0$ gives $x = -4$, and $x - 2 = 0$ gives $x = 2$. The $-3$ is $a$; it is not a zero.

m202-6-3-b.title: Quadratic Functions in Factored Form, Part 2: Axis, Vertex and Intercepts

cues.prompt: What is the vertex of $y = (x - 1)(x - 7)$?

m202-6-3-c.title: Quadratic Functions in Factored Form, Part 3: Writing Equations and Modelling Arches

cues.prompt: A parabola has zeros $0$ and $6$ and passes through $(2, 16)$. What is its equation?

m202-7-1.title: Solving Quadratic Equations by Graphing and Factoring, Part 1: Roots and Graphs

cues.prompt: The graph of $y = ax^2 + bx + c$ lies entirely above the $x$-axis. How many real roots does $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$ have?
cues.working: The roots are the $x$-intercepts. A graph entirely above the $x$-axis never meets it, so there are no real roots.

m202-7-1-b.title: Solving Quadratic Equations by Graphing and Factoring, Part 2: Solving by Factoring

chapters.title: Get zero on one side first

cues.prompt: Solve $x^2 - x = 12$.

m202-7-1-c.title: Solving Quadratic Equations by Graphing and Factoring, Part 3: Special Cases and Decomposition

m202-7-2.title: The Quadratic Formula, Part 1: Using the Formula

cues.prompt: Use the quadratic formula to solve $x^2 + 5x + 6 = 0$.

m202-7-2-b.title: The Quadratic Formula, Part 2: Decimal and Exact Roots

cues.prompt: Solve $3x^2 - 2x - 2 = 0$. Round to the nearest hundredth.
cues.working: $b^2 - 4ac = 4 + 24 = 28$, so $x = \dfrac{2 \pm \sqrt{28}}{6} \approx 1.22$ or $-0.55$. B uses $b$ instead of $-b$; C divides only the root by $6$; D divides by $2$, not $2a$.

m202-7-2-c.title: The Quadratic Formula, Part 3: How Many Roots, and Choosing a Method

cues.prompt: How many real roots does $4x^2 - 12x + 9 = 0$ have?
choices: It cannot be told without graphing.

m202-7-3.title: Solving Problems with Quadratic Equations, Part 1: A Plan for Problems

cues.prompt: A rectangle is $4$ m longer than it is wide. Its area is $60\ \text{m}^2$. How wide is it?
cues.working: $w(w + 4) = 60$, so $w^2 + 4w - 60 = 0$ and $(w + 10)(w - 6) = 0$. Reject $w = -10$: the width is $6$ m (and the length $10$ m).

m202-7-3-b.title: Solving Problems with Quadratic Equations, Part 2: Projectiles

cues.prompt: A ball’s height is $h = -4.9t^2 + 9.8t + 2$. When does it hit the ground? Round to the nearest hundredth of a second.
cues.working: $b^2 - 4ac = 96.04 + 39.2 = 135.24$, so $t = \dfrac{-9.8 \pm \sqrt{135.24}}{-9.8} \approx -0.19$ or $2.19$. Reject the negative time. C is when it is highest.

m202-7-3-c.title: Solving Problems with Quadratic Equations, Part 3: Borders and Break-Even Prices

chapters.title: A border goes on both sides

cues.prompt: A diagonal path across a rectangular plot is $13$ m long. One side is $7$ m longer than the other. Find the side lengths.

m202-8-1.title: Comparing and Interpreting Rates, Part 1: Unit Rates and Better Buys

cues.prompt: Juice costs \$3.29 for $1.89$ L or \$1.99 for $1$ L. Which has the lower price per litre?
choices: The $1.89$ L carton, at about \$1.74 per litre
The $1$ L carton, at \$1.99 per litre
They cost the same per litre.
The $1.89$ L carton, at about \$6.22 per litre
cues.working: \$3.29 ÷ 1.89 ≈ \$1.74 per litre, which is less than \$1.99 per litre. D multiplies instead of dividing.

m202-8-1-b.title: Comparing and Interpreting Rates, Part 2: Fuel Use and Rates as Slopes

cues.prompt: A van uses $9.4$ L/100 km and a hybrid uses $5.1$ L/100 km. Which statement is true?
choices: The van is more fuel-efficient, because $9.4 > 5.1$.
You cannot compare them without the distance.
cues.working: L/100 km measures fuel used, so a smaller number is better. The hybrid uses less fuel for every $100$ km.

m202-8-1-c.title: Comparing and Interpreting Rates, Part 3: Rates That Change

cues.prompt: On a graph of water in a tank against time, one segment is horizontal and another goes down steeply. What do they show?
choices: Horizontal: no change. Steep and down: draining quickly.
Horizontal: filling quickly. Steep and down: no change.
Horizontal: draining. Steep and down: filling.
cues.working: A horizontal segment has a rate of $0$, and a steep downward segment has a large negative rate: the amount of water drops quickly.

m202-8-2.title: Solving Problems with Rates, Part 1: Multiply or Divide by a Rate
